# package nmt

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/nmt"
```

Package nmt implements CANopen network management (CiA 301 7.2.8 and 7.3.2): NMT module control and NMT error control.

Module control:

  - [Master](#type-master) sends the NMT commands (start, stop, enter pre-operational, reset node, reset communication) to one node or to all.
  - [Slave](#type-slave) is a node's NMT state machine: boot-up message and Pre-operational after Start, the transitions the commands request, and the two resets, which restore the dictionary areas (reset node: 0x2000..0x9FFF and then 0x1000..0x1FFF; reset communication: 0x1000..0x1FFF), apply a pending node-ID and call a reset handler before the new boot-up message.

Error control:

  - [HeartbeatProducer](#type-heartbeatproducer) sends a node's state every producer heartbeat time (0x1017); a change of the period takes effect at once.
  - [HeartbeatConsumer](#type-heartbeatconsumer) tracks the state of every node, supervises the configured ones (explicitly, or from the consumer heartbeat time entries of 0x1016) and reports boot-ups, state changes, timeouts (once per loss) and resumption. [HeartbeatConsumer.WaitState](#func-heartbeatconsumer-waitstate) and [HeartbeatConsumer.WaitBootUp](#func-heartbeatconsumer-waitbootup) help an NMT master sequence its commands.
  - [GuardMaster](#type-guardmaster) and [GuardResponder](#type-guardresponder) implement the legacy node guarding and life guarding protocol (remote frames with a toggling state response).

Every long-running service has Start, which subscribes before it returns so that no frame is missed afterwards, and Close, which stops it and waits for its goroutine. Callbacks (handler options) run on the service's goroutine and must not block for long. Services configured [WithDictionary](#func-withdictionary) read their parameters from the standard objects and follow writes of them, as an SDO server makes them, while running.

```go
const Unconfigured canopen.NodeID = 0xFF
```

Unconfigured is the node-ID of a device whose node-ID is not configured yet (CiA 305: 0xFF, the value of lss.Unconfigured). A [Slave](#type-slave) with it stays in Initialising: it sends no boot-up message and executes only reset commands sent to all nodes, until a reset applies a configured pending node-ID ([Slave.SetNodeID](#func-slave-setnodeid), usually from LSS).

### type GuardMaster

```go
type GuardMaster struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

GuardMaster guards nodes with the legacy node guarding protocol (CiA 301 7.2.8.3.2.1): every guard time it sends a remote frame to 0x700 + node-ID and expects the node's state with an alternating toggle bit before the next request. A missing response or one with a wrong toggle bit is a miss; lifeTimeFactor consecutive misses (at least one) are a node guarding event (GuardTimeout).

The first response after Guard may have either toggle value; after a boot-up message the next one must have the toggle bit clear.

### type GuardResponder

```go
type GuardResponder struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

GuardResponder answers the node guarding requests of an NMT master for its node: each remote frame on 0x700 + node-ID gets the NMT state with a toggle bit that alternates, starting at 0 (and again at 0 after ResetToggle, which a reset communication calls for). Nothing is sent while the state is Initialising.

With a guard time and a life time factor configured it also does life guarding: after the first request, no request within guard time × life time factor is a life guarding event (GuardTimeout), reported once until the next request (GuardResumed).

CiA 301 does not allow node guarding and the heartbeat at once: run the responder only while the producer heartbeat time is 0.

### type HeartbeatConsumer

```go
type HeartbeatConsumer struct {

	// closed and replaced on every update
	// closed by Close

	// removes the 0x1016 write hook

}
```

HeartbeatConsumer receives the heartbeats and boot-up messages of all nodes (CiA 301 7.2.8.3.2.2), tracks every node's state and supervises the configured ones: a node whose heartbeat does not arrive within its consumer heartbeat time is reported lost once (EventTimeout) until it is heard again (EventResumed). As CiA 301 requires, supervision of a node starts with its first heartbeat, not with the configuration, and a boot-up message suspends it until the next heartbeat.

Node guarding responses (bit 7 toggling) are read as heartbeats with the toggle bit ignored.

Options: [WithLogger](#func-withlogger), [WithHeartbeatHandler](#func-withheartbeathandler), [WithDictionary](#func-withdictionary) (0x1016, which must exist; its write hook is registered at once and refuses duplicate node-IDs), [WithFD](#func-withfd).

### type HeartbeatProducer

```go
type HeartbeatProducer struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

HeartbeatProducer sends a node's heartbeat (CiA 301 7.2.8.3.2.2): its NMT state on 0x700 + node-ID every period. A period of 0 produces nothing. A new period takes effect at once: the next heartbeat follows the change by the new period.

The state comes from a function, usually [Slave.State](#func-slave-state); no heartbeat is sent while it returns Initialising (the slave is resetting and will send a boot-up message) or Unknown.

Periods are kept by a time.Ticker: heartbeats do not drift, but each one may be late by the scheduling latency of the Go runtime (typically well below a millisecond, more on a loaded system).

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*config)
```

Option configures the services of this package. Each option names the services it applies to; the others ignore it.

#### func WithBootUpHandler

```go
func WithBootUpHandler(h func()) Option
```

WithBootUpHandler calls h just before a [Slave](#type-slave) sends its boot-up message (at Start and after every reset), on the goroutine that sends it: the moment the node stops being Initialising, for services that must not act on frames received earlier. It must not block.

#### func WithDictionary

```go
func WithDictionary(d *od.Dictionary) Option
```

WithDictionary takes the service's parameters from an object dictionary and follows their changes:

  - [Slave](#type-slave): an NMT reset restores the dictionary's default values (reset node: 0x2000..0x9FFF, then 0x1000..0x1FFF; reset communication: 0x1000..0x1FFF) and applies a pending node-ID;
  - [HeartbeatProducer](#type-heartbeatproducer): the period is the producer heartbeat time 0x1017 (ms);
  - [HeartbeatConsumer](#type-heartbeatconsumer): the supervised nodes are the entries of the consumer heartbeat time 0x1016 (node-ID in bits 16..23, time in ms in bits 0..15), and writes that would supervise one node twice are refused with [canopen.AbortParamIncompatible](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortParamIncompatible);
  - [GuardResponder](#type-guardresponder): the life guarding parameters are the guard time 0x100C (ms) and the life time factor 0x100D.

#### func WithFD

```go
func WithFD(brs bool) Option
```

WithFD selects CANopen FD (CiA 1301), which carries every protocol in CAN FD frames (with bit rate switching when brs is true): a [Master](#type-master) sends its commands, a [Slave](#type-slave) its boot-up message and a [HeartbeatProducer](#type-heartbeatproducer) its heartbeats in CAN FD frames, and a [Slave](#type-slave) and a [HeartbeatConsumer](#type-heartbeatconsumer) accept CAN FD frames as well as classical ones (without the option they ignore CAN FD frames). The NMT protocols themselves are unchanged. Node guarding uses remote frames, which CAN FD does not have: [GuardMaster](#type-guardmaster) and [GuardResponder](#type-guardresponder) ignore the option and a CANopen FD device supervises with heartbeats only.

### type Slave

```go
type Slave struct {

	// serialises resets

	// 0: none

}
```

Slave is the NMT slave state machine of a node (CiA 301 7.3.2.2): Initialising, then (after the boot-up message) Pre-operational, and the transitions the NMT commands addressed to the node or to all nodes request. Reset node and reset communication pass through Initialising, restore the dictionary areas, call the reset handler and send a new boot-up message.

A Slave is safe for concurrent use. Its state is the state source of a [HeartbeatProducer](#type-heartbeatproducer) and a [GuardResponder](#type-guardresponder) ([Slave.State](#func-slave-state)).

```go
func NewSlave(bus canopen.Bus, node canopen.NodeID, opts ...Option) (*Slave, error)
```

NewSlave returns the NMT slave of a node, in state Initialising until Start. node is 1..127, or Unconfigured for a device that waits for its node-ID (LSS). Options: [WithLogger](#func-withlogger), [WithDictionary](#func-withdictionary), [WithStateHandler](#func-withstatehandler), [WithResetHandler](#func-withresethandler), [WithFD](#func-withfd).

#### func (Slave) NodeID

```go
func (s *Slave) NodeID() canopen.NodeID
```

NodeID returns the active node-ID.

#### func (Slave) Reset

```go
func (s *Slave) Reset(ctx context.Context, kind ResetKind) error
```

Reset does an NMT reset locally, as the command from the bus would: state Initialising, dictionary restore, reset handler, boot-up message, Pre-operational. It returns the error of sending the boot-up message (the slave then stays in Initialising) and [canopen.ErrClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#ErrClosed) after Close. A reset that leaves the node-ID Unconfigured ends in Initialising without boot-up message.

#### func (Slave) SetNodeID

```go
func (s *Slave) SetNodeID(node canopen.NodeID) error
```

SetNodeID sets a pending node-ID (as LSS configures one): it becomes active at the next reset communication or reset node, before the dictionary is restored, so that node-ID-relative defaults follow it. Unconfigured makes the node unconfigured at that reset (it then stays in Initialising).

#### func (Slave) SetState

```go
func (s *Slave) SetState(st canopen.NMTState) error
```

SetState changes the state locally (an application that enters Operational on its own, or stops after a fatal error). Only Stopped, Operational and Pre-operational can be set; use Reset for the others.

#### func (Slave) Start

```go
func (s *Slave) Start() error
```

Start subscribes to NMT commands, sends the boot-up message and enters Pre-operational, then executes received commands until Close. When the boot-up message cannot be sent, Start fails and the slave stays in Initialising. A slave whose node-ID is Unconfigured sends no boot-up message and stays in Initialising; the reset that applies its node-ID boots it.

#### func (Slave) State

```go
func (s *Slave) State() canopen.NMTState
```

State returns the current NMT state.

#### func (Slave) Stats

```go
func (s *Slave) Stats() SlaveStats
```

Stats returns the counters.

### type SlaveStats

```go
type SlaveStats struct {
	Commands uint64 `json:"commands"` // NMT commands executed
	Ignored  uint64 `json:"ignored"`  // commands for other nodes
	Invalid  uint64 `json:"invalid"`  // malformed NMT frames
	BootUps  uint64 `json:"bootUps"`  // boot-up messages sent
	Resets   uint64 `json:"resets"`   // resets done
}
```

SlaveStats counts what a [Slave](#type-slave) did.

### type StateChange

```go
type StateChange struct {
	Node canopen.NodeID   // the slave's node-ID after the change
	From canopen.NMTState // previous state
	To   canopen.NMTState // new state
	// Command is the NMT command that caused the change; 0 for a local
	// change (Start, SetState) and for the end of a reset (boot-up).
	Command canopen.NMTCommand
	Time    time.Time
}
```

StateChange reports a transition of a [Slave](#type-slave).
